data.title: Staff Digital Verification Engineer
data.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 

You Are

You have spent years building verification environments that have to catch the bugs no one else saw coming, the corner cases that only show up when three protocols collide and a timing edge goes the wrong way. You know that a test plan is only as good as the bugs it finds, and you have learned to think like the design, like the system integrator, and like the customer all at once. 

You are the engineer who sees a coverage hole at 95% and knows exactly which scenario is missing. Writing assertions is not a checkbox exercise for you, it is how you encode your understanding of what should never happen. You have debugged enough waveforms to know when something smells wrong three layers deeper than the symptom. 

Leading a verification effort means more than running regressions. You set the strategy, you review the test plans your team writes, and you make the call on what gets verified to what depth. You work directly with RTL designers and architects, not to rubber-stamp their work but to push back when the intent is unclear or the interface is going to be painful to verify. 

At Synopsys, you will work on DesignWare IP that ships into real products. The verification environments you build will be used across product generations, and the bugs you catch will never make it to silicon. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and evolve SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments for DesignWare synthesizable IP cores, ensuring they scale across multiple product generations and configurations
 - Define comprehensive test plans that cover corner cases, protocol compliance, and system-level interactions for serial interface protocols and memory controllers, including DDR and LPDDR where applicable
 - Write and debug complex testbenches, checkers, and assertions that catch real bugs in critical PHY blocks and interface logic
 - Develop software requirements for the PHY that scale across various configurations and use cases
 - Own verification closure for multiple critical blocks within DDR PHYs, including functional coverage, code coverage, and formal signoff
 - Collaborate directly with RTL designers, digital architects, and circuit teams to align verification scope with design intent and surface issues early in the design cycle
 - Manage regression infrastructure and work with the infra team to optimize verification cycles, debug failures, and keep the environment reliable

The Impact You Will Have

- Your verification environments will catch critical bugs before tapeout, directly affecting the quality and time-to-market of DesignWare IP used across the semiconductor industry
 - The test plans you define and review will set the verification standard for the team, ensuring consistent coverage and reducing escapes
 - Your coverage-driven approach will surface gaps that others miss, leading to more robust IP and fewer silicon respins
 - The assertions and checkers you write will become reusable verification IP, accelerating future projects and raising the quality bar
 - Your collaboration with RTL and architecture teams will shape design decisions early, making designs easier to verify and more reliable in the field
 - The regression strategies you implement will directly improve team productivity and reduce verification cycle time
 - Your ownership of critical PHY blocks will ensure that high-stakes features meet functional and performance requirements on schedule

What You'll Need

- Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering or Electronics and Communication Engineering with 4+ years of hands-on verification experience
 - Proven track record leading verification teams through IP project delivery, including planning, execution, and signoff
 - Strong experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches from scratch and evolving them as designs grow in complexity
 - Deep expertise writing test plans, implementing checkers, and building assertions that catch real bugs, not just toggle coverage
 - Proficiency extracting and interpreting functional coverage and code coverage metrics, and using those insights to drive verification closure
 - Experience verifying serial interface protocols and working through IP design and verification processes, knowledge of DDR or LPDDR protocols is a strong plus
 - Demonstrated ability to own end-to-end verification deliverables, including metric closure and formal review signoff, experience with AI-assisted verification tools is a plus

Who You Are

- You can walk into a coverage review, spot the gap in the test plan, and articulate exactly what scenario is missing and why it matters
 - You write assertions that encode real design intent, not just the obvious cases, and you know the difference between a checker that catches bugs and one that just makes noise
 - You are comfortable leading technical discussions with RTL designers and architects, pushing back when verification scope is unclear or the interface is going to create downstream pain
 - You manage multiple verification efforts in parallel without losing track of what is at risk, what is on schedule, and what needs attention today
 - You debug with purpose, you do not just stare at waveforms hoping for insight, you form hypotheses, test them, and move systematically toward root cause
 - You treat verification infrastructure as a product, you care about regression efficiency, debug turnaround time, and whether your environment is actually usable by the rest of the team

The Team You'll Be Part Of

Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process. 

Rewards and Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

data.title: Head of Injection Moulding (Mobile Industry)
data.description:
HEAD OF INJECTION MOULDING

Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech or Diploma - Plastics, Polymer, Mechanical or Production Engineering Mobile handset industry moulding experience is mandatory - please read below before applying

Moulding is where our product starts, and where our cost is set. A part moulded badly becomes a part printed badly, assembled badly and rejected at pack - by which point we've paid for all of it. 

You'd own moulding as a function: the floor, the process, the people, the capacity and the capital. That includes overmoulding - rigid shell with soft-touch elastomer - which is a meaningful part of what we produce and a materially harder process than single-shot. 

We are only considering candidates from the mobile handset industry

We want to be direct about this so nobody wastes their time. 

We make small, cosmetically critical parts - sub-millimetre wall sections, visible surfaces with no tolerance for sink or flow marks, tight fit against a device, and cosmetic standards closer to consumer electronics than to general plastics. A part that would pass in most moulding shops gets rejected here. 

The discipline that produces that output is learned in the handset supply chain, and it doesn't transfer quickly from elsewhere. Excellent moulding experience in automotive, appliance, packaging, housewares or general engineering plastics is genuinely excellent experience - it just isn't what this role needs, and we'd be setting you up to struggle. 

So: you should have spent meaningful time moulding handset housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures - at Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, Transsion, Foxconn, Dixon, Lava or in their tier-one supplier base. Adjacent consumer electronics enclosure work at the same cosmetic standard will also be considered. 

The thing that actually limits this floor

We're high-mix. Many moulds, frequent changes, moderate volume per run. In that environment the constraint usually isn't cycle time - it's changeover and the scrap that follows it. Every tool change costs setup hours, then costs more shots before the process stabilises. Across a week of changes that's a serious share of capacity spent producing nothing. 

Most moulding operations measure cycle time obsessively and changeover barely at all. We'd like someone who goes after it. 

What you'd build

- Changeover discipline - SMED method, prepared tooling, parallel setup, and a measured changeover time that comes down
 - Validated parameter sets per mould, so a setter isn't rediscovering the process each time, and a first-off routine that reaches stable quickly and records what stable looked like
 - Material handling discipline - polymer dried to spec before it goes near a machine. Wet resin causes splay and cosmetic defects that get blamed on printing two stations later
 - A skill matrix for setters and operators, with certification before anyone runs unsupervised, and cross-training so capacity doesn't depend on one person's attendance
 - Real downtime and scrap data coded by cause, so improvement has something to aim at
 - Capacity planning and the case for new machines as we grow

You'd own

- Moulding production across shifts, against the plan
 - Scrap and first-pass yield at the machine. Your primary number
 - Process capability, parameter control and changeover performance
 - Machine utilisation, uptime and maintenance coordination
 - Tool condition in production - shot counts, preventive maintenance schedules, spare inserts and components, and escalation to the tool room before a tool fails rather than after
 - Tool repair and refurbishment decisions, with the cost case
 - Moulding capacity decisions and capital proposals
 - The moulding team - setters, operators, helpers, supervisors - including hiring and training
 - Safety, 5S and housekeeping

You need

- 12+ years in injection moulding, with function or plant-level ownership rather than shift supervision alone
 - Mobile handset moulding experience - mandatory. Housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures, at a handset OEM or in their tier-one supplier base. See the note above
 - Hands-on process capability. You can set a machine, read a short shot, and tell a setter what to change and why
 - Defect diagnosis: short shot, flash, sink, weld lines, warpage, splay, burn marks - cause, not just name
 - Material knowledge - PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, PP and filled grades; drying requirements, moisture sensitivity, masterbatch and regrind Overmoulding. A real part of our production and not a side skill: 
 - Two-shot and insert moulding - rotary platen, index and core-back methods, or mould-and-transfer. The machine and tool requirements of each, and when one suits better than the other
 - Material pairing and bond - which combinations bond chemically, which need mechanical interlock, and how melt temperature, shore hardness and surface condition affect adhesion. TPU and TPE over PC and PC/ABS specifically
 - Bond strength as an invisible defect. An overmoulded part can look perfect and delaminate weeks later in a customer's hand. It has to be designed and processed right, because inspection won't catch it. Peel and bond testing is part of the job, not an afterthought
 - Differential shrinkage and warpage between the two materials, and first-shot dimensional stability before the second shot
 - Cycle balancing - the slower shot sets the cycle, which makes process optimisation here a different problem from single-shot
 - Interface flash, colour bleed and the cosmetic defects specific to two-material parts

Tooling, in detail. This is not a nice-to-have for us: 

- Tool construction - mould base and insert construction, steel grades and hardness, cold and hot runner systems, gate types and vestige, cooling layout and what it does to cycle and warpage, venting, ejection, slides and lifters, shut-off surfaces, surface finish and texture
 - Two-shot tool construction - rotation and indexing, sealing at the material interface, second-shot shut-offs, and why these tools fail differently from single-shot ones
 - Tool condition on the floor - reading flash as parting line wear, galling on slides, blocked vents causing burns, scaled water lines quietly adding seconds to cycle, ejector wear, hot runner tip and heater faults. Catching these before they become a stoppage or a scrap run
 - Trials and correction - T0/T1/T2, reading trial results, steel-safe versus steel-removal corrections, shrinkage adjustment, and knowing when a correction is worth doing
 - Repair, refurbish or replace, with the judgement and the cost case behind each
 - The arbitration. The most valuable thing you'll do is decide whether a defect is a tool problem or a process problem. Process people blame the tool, tool rooms blame the process, and the part keeps failing while they argue. We want someone who settles it with evidence
 - Demonstrated changeover or scrap reduction with numbers. We'll ask for before and after
 - Team building across shifts, including developing setters
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: tool room or tool design background earlier in your career, scientific moulding or DOE training, multi-cavity and high-cavitation tooling, IMD/IML, take-out robots and automation, SMED implementation, CIPET background, OEE systems. 

Where this sits alongside our Tooling Engineer: they own mould design review and new tool development; you own tools in production - condition, maintenance, correction and when to retire them. You'll disagree occasionally, and that's healthy. 

Tell us: which handset programmes or customers you moulded for, your overmoulding experience and the material pairs you've run, your average changeover time and what you did to it, your scrap rate and how it was measured, one defect where you proved it was the tool and not the process (or the reverse) and how you proved it, and the cosmetic standard you worked to.

data.title: Head of Printing
data.description:
Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech - Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production

Printing is the step that makes our product ours. It's also where most of our quality risk sits, because a defect found at pack is a part we've already paid to mould. 

Your scope is everything that happens to a part after it leaves the tool: UV printing, dye-sublimation, cylindrical and bottle printing, coating, and assembly - through to a finished product ready to pack. 

We have shift managers running the floor, an engineer keeping machines healthy, and a specialist owning colour. What we don't have is anyone accountable for whether our decoration as a whole is good and getting better - or for deciding what we should be able to produce two years from now. 

This role is technical before it is managerial. If you can't stand at a press and tell us why the part in your hand failed, the rest of the job won't work. 

And a large share of the time, the answer isn't the press. Adhesion failures usually trace back to materials - mould release contamination on the part surface, a substrate whose surface energy was never going to accept ink without treatment, plasticiser migrating out of a TPU weeks after it shipped. We want someone who looks upstream before blaming the machine. 

Who owns what - read this

Several roles touch printing, and all of them sit under you: 

- You own the outcome - print and assembly quality, process capability, and what we can and can't produce
 - Operations Managers own daily throughput and dispatch on their shifts
 - The UV Printing Engineer owns machine condition, maintenance and uptime
 - The Colour Management Specialist owns profiles and colour standards

When a defect appears, the diagnosis crosses all four. You decide where it actually came from, what changes, and you're accountable if it comes back. 

What you'd build

- Validated recipes per product and substrate across every process, so output doesn't depend on who's on shift
 - A process capability baseline - what our defect rates actually are, by type and by process. Harder to establish than it sounds, and impossible to improve without
 - A qualification route for new substrates and products, so new product development gets a real answer on printability and assembly rather than an opinion
 - Technology strategy: which process suits which product, where current capability runs out, and what we invest in next
 - A capability roadmap that lets us say yes to work we currently have to decline

Building the team

We're scaling, and most of our operators arrive without print-specific skills. How you build capability matters as much as how you build process. 

- A skill matrix per process - who can set up, who can run, who can judge quality on UV, sublimation, cylindrical and assembly. Certification before anyone operates unsupervised
 - Cross-training as a capacity lever, not an HR nicety. In high-mix production, if one person can set up the bottle line then that line's availability equals their attendance. Depth on every process is how we stop losing days to one person's leave
 - Limit samples, so "acceptable" is a physical object an operator can hold rather than an opinion that shifts by shift. Most quality arguments on a print floor are really definition arguments
 - Train-the-trainer, so capability multiplies rather than routing through you
 - A progression path that gives a good operator a reason to stay beyond the next ₹2, 000 offer
 - The structure of the function itself as we grow - shift coverage, technical specialists, quality

You'd own

- UV flatbed, cylindrical and bottle printing, dye-sublimation, coating and assembly
 - Quality and first-pass yield across the whole post-moulding chain. The number this role is judged on
 - Capacity planning against the production plan
 - Capital decisions for new capacity, and the business cases behind them
 - Customer complaints through to root cause and corrective action
 - The function and its team: shift operations, machine engineering, colour

You need

Real technical depth across our processes. Specifically: 

- Dye-sublimation - transfer printing onto polyester and poly-coated substrates, heat press and 3D vacuum sublimation, and how time, temperature and pressure shift the final result
 - UV inkjet - flatbed printing, LED curing, primer and surface preparation, white ink and varnish layers, and adhesion that holds up weeks later rather than just at inspection
 - Cylindrical and bottle printing - rotary setup, chuck alignment, tapered and non-uniform profiles, maintaining head gap over a curved surface
 - Assembly - multi-part products, fit and tolerance, insert handling, and cosmetic damage prevention on finished parts

Materials - plastics. How substrate behaviour decides what decoration is possible: PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, TPE, PP, PMMA and filled grades. Surface energy and dyne level, and which plastics need corona, plasma or flame treatment before they'll accept anything. Heat deflection limits, which govern what can be sublimated without distorting the part. Mould release carryover, plasticiser migration, and the other upstream causes of a print that fails three weeks later. 

Materials - coatings. Hard coat, soft-touch and PU systems, UV-curable versus two-component thermal cure. Primer and adhesion promoter selection. Mix ratio, pot life and cure schedules for 2K systems. Order of operations - coating over print versus print over coating - and why that choice is rarely reversible. Coating defects: orange peel, fish eyes, pinholes, poor levelling. 

Testing. Cross-hatch adhesion, abrasion, chemical and sweat resistance, and accelerated ageing - enough to establish whether a finish actually holds rather than assuming it will. 

Plus: 

- An engineering degree. B. E. /B. Tech in Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production. Printing Technology and Polymer Engineering map most closely to this role; a CIPET background is directly relevant on the materials side
 - 12+ years in industrial or digital printing production, with genuine function ownership rather than supervision alone
 - Defect diagnosis you can demonstrate - separating machine, ink, substrate, file, operator and environment as causes rather than guessing
 - Colour management fundamentals, fluent enough to challenge the specialist who owns them
 - Quality improvement with numbers - a defect rate you reduced, and how
 - Equipment selection and commissioning, with capital accountability
 - Demonstrated team building - you've hired, structured and grown a production team, not just inherited one
 - A training system you built, with evidence it worked: skill matrices, certification, limit samples, or whatever you used
 - Leadership across shifts and across technical specialists who know their speciality better than you do
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: injection moulding exposure, coating line operation, metals and glass decoration, high-mix short-run environments, screen or pad printing, IMD/IML, drinkware or promotional product decoration. 

Tell us: one print defect you root-caused where the obvious answer turned out to be wrong, one adhesion or coating failure you traced to a material cause, one quality metric you moved with before and after numbers, one operator you developed into something more, and the specific processes, substrates and coatings you've personally run.

Job Description

We are seeking a versatile and highly skilled Lead AI/ML Engineer with deep expertise in Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs). This role requires a leader who can take full ownership of the AI lifecycle - from initial architectural design to final production execution. You will lead the development of scalable AI-powered applications, demonstrating exceptional execution skills and the ability to deliver high-performance results under pressure in demanding production environments. 

Machine Learning & LLM Capability

- End-to-End ML Engineering : Build and manage comprehensive ML pipelines, including data ingestion, preprocessing, training, and evaluation using frameworks like PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Scikit-learn. 
 - Advanced LLM Systems : Design and implement sophisticated LLM-based applications such as autonomous agents, chatbots, and complex automation tools. 
 - Generative AI Specialization : Architect and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines using vector databases like FAISS, Pinecone, or Weaviate. 
 - Model Optimization : Fine-tune open-source and proprietary models (e. g. , LLaMA, GPT) using advanced techniques like LoRA, QLoRA, or instruction tuning. 
 - Agentic Frameworks : Develop complex agentic workflows utilizing frameworks such as LangChain or LlamaIndex. 
 - Prompt Engineering : Implement expert-level prompt engineering, tool/function calling, and structured output generation. 

Project Ownership & Execution

- Full Lifecycle Ownership : Take complete accountability for the full ML and GenAI lifecycle, spanning data processing, model development, monitoring, and optimization. 
 - Architectural Leadership : Drive strategic architectural decisions for AI platforms, ensuring they are modular, scalable, and maintainable. 
 - Execution Excellence : Write clean, high-performance Python code following strict OOP principles and manage CI/CD pipelines for seamless project execution. 
 - Leadership & Mentoring : Act as a key technical leader, managing stakeholders and mentoring team members to ensure all project milestones are met with quality. 
 - System Integrity : Manage model and prompt versioning, experiment tracking, and comprehensive documentation for all pipelines and workflows. 

Performance Under Pressure

- Production Reliability : Ensure all AI systems maintain extreme scalability and performance under heavy production workloads, including both batch and real-time processing. 
 - High-Pressure Optimization : Rapidly optimize inference latency and system costs for ML and LLM systems to meet urgent business and technical requirements. 
 - Proactive Problem Solving : Apply strong analytical thinking to address complex challenges such as system drift, hallucinations, and latency in fast-paced environments. 
 - Robust Guardrails : Implement and manage strict evaluation frameworks and feedback loops to maintain system quality under stress.

This role leads development of event‐driven data architectures, CDC frameworks, data lake ingestion pipelines, and scalable ETL/ELT processes. data.description:
BUREAU VERITAS | HR SHARED SERVICES HUB, NOIDA

Service Delivery Manager - Performance & Continuous Improvement

Intelligent Command Centre (ICC) & Transformation Lead - all towers

Tower

Cross-tower: Performance, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Location

Noida, India (HR Shared Services Hub)

Reports to

HR SSC Regional Hub Director, Noida

Role type

People manager

Scope

Intelligent Command Centre, SLA and KPI governance, continuous improvement portfolio, transition PMO support and hub quality management

Grade

About The Hub

Bureau Veritas is building a greenfield HR Shared Services hub in Noida. The hub will bring HR operations that currently run separately in each country into one standardised, digitally enabled service centre. You will design your tower, move work into Noida in structured waves, and run it at scale to global standards. 

ROLE PURPOSE

You are the hub's performance and improvement engine. You will build the Intelligent Command Centre that gives leaders one real-time view of service health across every tower. You will also run the continuous improvement system that moves the hub from stable operations to best-in-class service. 

Key Responsibilities

- Transition and shared services set-up
 - Design the hub's performance framework: a KPI tree, SLA definitions, data sources and a reporting cadence shared by all towers. 
 - Capture and certify the pre-transition baselines for each country, so the hub can prove its value against the starting point. 
 - Support the transition PMO with readiness scorecards, go/no-go dashboards and hypercare tracking for every wave. 
 - Set up the Intelligent Command Centre, covering architecture, data pipelines, dashboards and alerting. 
 - Process ownership and service delivery
 - Run the ICC day to day, with real-time SLA, volume, backlog and escalation monitoring across R2P, R2H, Q2R and A2W. 
 - Lead the hub's governance rhythm: daily stand-ups, weekly tower reviews, monthly service reviews and quarterly business reviews with stakeholders. 
 - Own the hub-wide customer voice programme, including CSAT and NPS surveys, closing the loop with respondents, and reporting insight. 
 - Run hub-level capacity and productivity analytics to support resourcing decisions. 
 - Governance, risk and controls
 - Own the hub quality management system, covering process documentation standards, internal quality audits and control testing across towers. 
 - Maintain the hub risk register and the tracking of issues and actions. 
 - Build data governance for performance reporting so that there is one version of the truth. 
 - Continuous improvement and digital
 - Build and govern the hub-wide continuous improvement backlog. Prioritise by value and effort, and agree ownership with each GPO. 
 - Lead improvement projects using Lean, Six Sigma and process mining. Track benefits through to realised savings. 
 - Run the hub's automation and AI pipeline, from idea intake to business case, delivery and benefits tracking. 
 - Build a continuous improvement culture through training, recognition and a simple way for every employee to raise ideas. 
 - People leadership, performance and culture
 - Build the tower's team from the ground up. Define the structure, spans of control, role profiles and hiring plan for each transition wave. 
 - Recruit, onboard and develop team leads and specialists. Build succession cover for every critical role before the tower reaches steady state. 
 - Run a disciplined people-performance cycle covering goal setting, monthly one-to-ones, quarterly reviews and calibrated year-end ratings. 
 - Keep attrition, absence and engagement at or better than hub targets. Act early on hotspots. 
 - Model the hub culture of ownership, customer focus, speed with control and learning. Make it visible in how the team works every day. 
 - Build capability through skills matrices, cross-training and certification paths. Create career moves across towers. 

What Success Looks Like

- First 90 days: hub KPI framework, baseline method and ICC design signed off. 
 - By go-live: ICC live with real-time dashboards for the first transition wave, and the governance rhythm running. 
 - Within 12-18 months: continuous improvement portfolio delivering measurable, validated benefits, with hub-wide dashboards trusted by global stakeholders. 

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

KPI

Indicative target

Hub-wide SLA adherence

≥ 95% across towers

Validated CI Benefits

Annual savings and hours released against target

Automation hours released

Increased year on year

Reporting timeliness and accuracy

100% on schedule

Hub CSAT / NPS

At or above target

Audit and quality findings

Closed within agreed timelines

CI participation

% of employees who submitted or delivered an improvement

Targets are indicative. They will be finalised in the hub SLA framework and country baselines. 

Technical Skills

- Performance management and command-centre design for multi-tower shared services. 
 - Lean Six Sigma methods, including DMAIC, value-stream mapping and root-cause analysis. 
 - Data analytics and visualisation (Power BI or Tableau). SQL or data-modelling skills are an advantage. 
 - Process mining (Celonis, Signavio or similar) and automation pipeline management (RPA, AI). 
 - ITIL service level management and quality management systems. 
 - Benefits realisation and business case development. 

LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

Customer-centric leadership

- Builds teams from zero
 - Drives change and adoption
 - Sound judgement under pressure
 - Influences without authority across countries
 - Data-led decision making
 - Coaches and develops talent
 - Holds a high bar on control

Essential

EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

- 15+ years of experience, including 7+ years in shared services performance, excellence or transformation roles. 
 - Has built and run an ICC, command centre or equivalent governance function. 
 - Has deployed continuous improvement frameworks across multi-tower shared services centres. 
 - Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 
 - Master's degree in Business, HR, Engineering or a related field. 

Preferred

- Transition PMO experience
 - Process mining certification
 - Change management certification (Prosci or equivalent)

KEY STAKEHOLDERS

Hub Director, all tower GPOs, Global HR leadership, HR technology and data teams, Finance, Internal Audit, transformation partners.

About the role

You will be the architect who wins the technical deal. Before a contract is signed, you show enterprise customers that their AI agents will work, at their scale and under their rules. You build the demos and proofs of concept, answer the architecture questions, and hand delivery a plan they can execute. This is a hands-on engineering role in front of customers. You write code most weeks and spend the rest with CIOs, platform teams and risk officers. You report to the Co-Founder and CTO. 

What you will do

• Discover: run technical discovery with CIOs, platform-engineering and risk teams at banks, insurers and asset managers. Map their systems, data and controls to the agent use cases that matter. 

• Demo: build tailored demos of agent workflows, using the customer's own scenarios where you can. 

• Prove: scope and deliver 2 to 6 week proofs of concept. Write the code, wire up integrations and measure results against agreed success criteria. 

• Design: produce reference architectures for agent deployment on AWS, Azure or GCP, covering identity, data access, observability and guardrails. 

• De-risk: answer security, compliance and model-risk questionnaires (SOC 2, data residency, audit logging, human-in-the-loop controls). 

• Hand off: turn every won proof of concept into a delivery plan our forward-deployed engineers can run from day one. 

• Feed back: bring field patterns to product and build reusable demo assets, templates and starter agents. 

What we are looking for

• 8+ years in software engineering, solutions engineering, solutions architecture or forward-deployed engineering for enterprise customers. 

• Hands-on experience building LLM applications or agents: prompt and tool design, RAG, evaluation, and at least one agent framework. 

• Strong Python, plus working knowledge of APIs, containers and one major cloud. 

• Comfort in regulated environments, where governance, auditability and access control decide the deal. 

• Consulting experience: client-facing work, scoping engagements and running workshops with enterprise stakeholders. 

• Understanding of tool calling and MCP, guardrails and policy controls, access management, observability and audit trails. 

Nice to have

• Experience selling to, or working inside, financial services. 

• Kubernetes, observability or AIOps tooling. 

• AWS, Azure or GCP certifications. 

• A public demo, repo, talk or post about something you built with agents. 

Location: Chennai, India (Chennai office), hybrid 3 days on-site, with travel to customer sites as needed. 

About Moring

Moring helps enterprises put AI agents into production safely.

data.description:
Job Description

Goldman Sachs Electronic Market Making - Software Engineer - Vice President - Bengaluru

The Electronic Market Making Cash Trading team systematically provides liquidity in US Equities and ETFs, both on-exchange and to low-touch client flow. The team leverages quantitative research combined with low-latency trading infrastructure to develop and implement automated trading and risk management strategies. We're a small team that demands a high level of ownership and accountability from each contributor, while strongly emphasizing collaboration and transparency. Engineers on the team are deeply involved in both software and strategy development. We are seeking a dedicated and ambitious engineer who thrives in a challenging environment and wants to make a meaningful impact at the firm. 

Your Impact

You will be working on building and enhancing platforms focused on electronic trading, market making and execution. You will work with other engineers and trading teams to improve all aspects of execution, price-making and risk management. You'll do this with a keen eye on performance, guided by a robust measurement framework and lots of experimentation. You will have an opportunity to develop a deep understanding of how GS interacts with some of the most dynamic and liquid markets in the world. 

Responsibilities

Design, build and maintain high performance, low latency trading platform which can evolve and adapt to changes in our fast-paced, global business environment. 

Analyze trading system performance and identify areas for improvement. 

Generate ideas for system enhancements that drive commercial performance. 

Implement, test and deploy these ideas. 

Improve the safety and reliability of trading systems. 

Manage work to balance the short-term needs of the business with strategic enhancements. 

Understand global market structure, regulations and exchange requirements. 

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor/Master's degree in STEM with 5 to 10 years of experience developing software architecture in C/ C++

Strong track record of designing, developing and maintaining reliable trading components and critical infrastructure

A deep passion for technology and software development

Sound understanding of multi-threaded application design and development and experience with lock-free data structures

Professional experience working with distributed systems

Knowledge of CPU microarchitecture, caches and memory subsystems and experience with micro-optimizations

Experience in low latency messaging, TCP/UDP tuning, Linux latency tunings is preferred

Experience with low latency trading platform is preferable but not necessary

Excellent communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with statistics and data-science methodologies

Experience with Python and data-science packages (e. g. numpy, scikit-learn)

Experience building and maintaining high-performance research infrastructure for large data inputs

Goldman Sachs Engineering Culture

At Goldman Sachs, our Engineers don't just make things - we make things possible. Change the world by connecting people and capital with ideas. Solve the most challenging and pressing engineering problems for our clients. Join our engineering teams that build massively scalable software and systems, architect low latency infrastructure solutions, proactively guard against cyber threats, and leverage machine learning alongside financial engineering to continuously turn data into action. Create new businesses, transform finance, and explore a world of opportunity at the speed of markets. 

Engineering is at the critical center of our business, and our dynamic environment requires innovative strategic thinking and immediate, real solutions. Want to push the limit of digital possibilities? Start here.

data.title: VP, eGRC Solution Architect (L12)
data.description:
Role Title: VP, eGRC Solution Architect (L12)

Company Overview

Synchrony (NYSE: SYF) is a leading consumer financing company that has been at the heart of American commerce and opportunity for nearly a century. Synchrony delivers credit and banking products that empower tens of millions of consumers to improve their financial lives and access what matters most. Leveraging innovative solutions that are shaping the future of retail commerce, Synchrony supports the growth and success of some of the nation's most respected brands, alongside hundreds of thousands of small and midsize businesses, including health and wellness providers. Committed to excellence in service and culture, Synchrony is proud to be named as #3 as a Great Place to Work® in India and is honored to be ranked the #1 Best Company to Work For® in the U. S. by Fortune magazine and Great Place to Work®. For more information, visit www. synchrony. com. 

Organizational Overview

Synchrony's Risk Team provides independent oversight of Synchrony's risk-taking activities to ensure safety and soundness, meet regulatory and legal requirements, and manage risks to the risk-appetite of the Board. Risk is responsible for independently assessing, quantifying, and overseeing risks & providing effective challenge . Risk serves as Synchrony's Second Line of Defense. 

Overall, Risk Team oversees and manages the Risk Program to support the business in anticipating and addressing risks, issues and challenges. Results are consistent with the respective strategic uses and complying with related overall risk, risk testing policies, standards, procedures as well as regulations. Our Risk organization consists of 4 pillars: Compliance, Credit & Financial Risk, Enterprise Risk and Operational Risk. Each of the pillars play a vital role in managing Risk and supports the business in anticipating and addressing risks, issues, and challenges. 

Role Summary/ Purpose

The eGRC Solution Architect is an individual contributor who partners with one or more Agile teams within the Risk Infrastructure delivery team to support Risk & Compliance stakeholder s . This role translates enterprise GRC objectives into technology solutions that automate, standardize, and integrate governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance processes. The architect designs end-to-end solutions, decomposes complex objectives into actionable deliverables, evaluates and aligns technical standards and tools, and provides technical leadership across the full delivery lifecycle. 

Key Responsibilities

- Design and deliver GRC solutions: Serve as the GRC technical architecture lead supporting multiple concurrent initiatives, designing end-to-end solutions that span GRC functions, provide design guidance, conduct architecture reviews, and resolving complex technical decisions. 
 - Translate requirements into technical solutions: Work with stakeholders, including Risk and Compliance leaders , to understand GRC requirements and translate them into actionable, technology-based solutions . 
 - Lead technical implementations : Guide and support development teams and related technical resources through the configuration and deployment of GRC software platforms. 
 - Provide technical and architectural guidance: Serve as the subject matter expert for GRC frameworks, processes (e. g. , RCSA, Issue Management, Compliance Risk Assessments), enabling technologies, and industry best practices. Partner with business stakeholders and technical teams to translate requirements into scalable solutions; lead architecture/design reviews; mentor teammates ; and maintain architecture diagrams and technical documentation. 
 - Manage project oversight: Oversee the technical vision of GRC projects, ensuring delivery excellence, security, and sustainability while also managing timelines, scope, and resources alongside project managers. 

Required Skills/Knowledge

- Bachelor's Degree and 10 +years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience or in lieu of degree High School Diploma/GED 12+ years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience
 - Deep GRC domain knowledge: Strong understanding of GRC concepts and core processes (e. g. , RCSA, Issue Management, Compliance Risk Assessments) and how they align to risk and control objectives . 
 - GRC platform expertise : 5+ years of hands-on advanced configuration/development experience with leading GRC platforms , including ServiceNow IRM, Archer , SAI360 . 
 - Solution architecture experience: 5+ years designing and delivering end-to-end GRC solutions on ServiceNow, Archer, or SAI360, including target-state architecture, standards, and non-functional requirements. 
 - Problem-solving and analytical skills: Proven ability to assess business needs, evaluate risk and control impacts, identify trade-offs, and design scalable solutions that meet functional requirements. 

Desired Skills/Knowledge

- Architectural and technical skills: Proficiency in designing complex systems, cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP), and enterprise integration via APIs and data pipelines. 
 - Communication and stakeholder management: The ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership. 

Eligibility Criteria

- Bachelor's Degree and 10 +years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience or in lieu of degree High School Diploma/GED 12+ years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience

Work Timings: 2: 30 PM to 11: 30 PM IST

We are proud to offer flexibility at Synchrony. Our way of working allows you the option to work from home or workspaces in our Regional Engagement Hubs-Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Kolkata, or Delhi/NCR. 

Occasionally you may be required to commute or travel to Hyderabad or one of the Regional Engagement Hubs for in person engagement activities such as business or team meetings, trainings, and culture events. 

For Internal Applicants

- Understand the criteria or mandatory skills required for the role, before applying. 
 - Inform your Manager or HRM before applying for any role on Workday. 
 - Ensure that your Professional Profile is updated (fields such as Education, Prior experience, Other skills) and it is mandatory to upload your updated resume (Word or PDF format) 
 - Must not be any corrective action plan (First Formal/Final Formal LPP)
 - L10+ Employees who have completed 18 months in the organization and 12 months in current role and level are only eligible. 
 - L10+ Employees can apply

Grade/Level: 12

Job Family Group

Risk Management

Job Title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (MERN/ Python)

Company: Codewinglet Pvt Ltd

Location: Surat, Gujarat (Must be based in Surat or willing to relocate)

Work Mode: Work from Office (WFO)

Experience: 2-4 Years

Employment Type: Full-time

About Codewinglet

Codewinglet Pvt. Ltd. is an AI-first engineering company building modern software products and solutions across AI, web, backend, and cloud technologies. 

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer from either a MERN or Python background who can own the building, improvement, and maintenance of scalable web applications across the Frontend, Backend, API, and Database layers. 

This role suits someone who enjoys solving complex technical problems, can own features independently from development to delivery, and wants to work closely with developers, QA, product, and engineering teams. 

Key Responsibilities

- Design, develop, and maintain scalable web applications using the MERN stack or Python-based stacks (Django / FastAPI / Flask with React. js). 
 - Own features and modules end-to-end, from requirement understanding and implementation to testing, deployment, and maintenance. 
 - Build responsive, reusable, high-performance UIs using React. js / Next. js with TypeScript. 
 - Develop secure, scalable backend services and RESTful APIs using Node. js/Express. js or Python frameworks. 
 - Design and optimize data models, queries, and indexes across MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and Redis. 
 - Integrate frontend applications with backend services, third-party APIs, and AI/LLM capabilities. 
 - Containerize applications with Docker and maintain CI/CD pipelines on cloud platforms. 
 - Write unit and integration tests to keep code reliable. 
 - Debug and resolve bugs, performance bottlenecks, and production issues. 
 - Conduct code reviews and give constructive technical feedback. 
 - Work in Agile/Scrum with QA, Project Managers, and other engineering teams to plan and deliver features. 
 - Contribute to technical discussions and implementation and design decisions. 
 - Guide junior developers through code reviews and knowledge sharing. 
 - Keep up with relevant technologies and help improve development practices. 

Must-Have Skills And Qualifications

- 2-4 years of hands-on Full Stack Web Development experience. 
 - Strong expertise in at least one stack: 
 - MERN: MongoDB, Express. js, React. js, Node. js, OR
 - Python: Django / FastAPI / Flask with React. js
 - Strong React. js skills: components, hooks, state management, reusable UI development. 
 - Hands-on experience with TypeScript and Next. js (or another modern React framework). 
 - Good understanding of MongoDB and PostgreSQL, plus working experience with Redis. 
 - Experience developing and integrating RESTful APIs. 
 - Exposure to AI/LLM integrations or AI-powered applications. 
 - Working knowledge of Docker and CI/CD practices. 
 - Experience with at least one cloud platform: AWS, Azure, or GCP. 
 - Experience writing unit and integration tests. 
 - Experience working in Agile/Scrum teams. 
 - Experience conducting code reviews and mentoring junior developers. 
 - Good understanding of Git and collaborative development workflows. 
 - Strong debugging, problem-solving, and analytical skills. 
 - Ability to own tasks independently and deliver on time. 
 - Strong communication skills and ability to work with technical and cross-functional teams. 
Good to Have

- Experience building MVPs, POCs, or demos to support product launches or client pitches. 
 - Experience implementing product analytics or event tracking (GA4, Mixpanel, PostHog) to measure feature adoption. 
 - Experience building go-to-market features such as user onboarding flows or payment/subscription integrations (Stripe, Razorpay). 

What You'll Gain?

- End-to-end ownership of features across Frontend, Backend, API, and Database. 
 - Work on modern products and real-world engineering challenges. 
 - Exposure to AI, GenAI, and AI-powered applications in an AI-first environment. 
 - A voice in technical decisions, architecture discussions, and development practices. 
 - Close collaboration with developers, QA, product, and technical leadership. 
 - Opportunities to mentor engineers while growing your own expertise. 

Why Join Codewinglet?

- Modern products and technologies in an AI-first engineering environment. 
 - Real-time AI projects, including AI Agents and GenAI systems. 
 - High-growth, fast-paced learning environment. 
 - Exposure to the latest technologies and live projects. 
 - Supportive and transparent leadership. 
 - Clear career growth and performance-based appraisals. 
 - Competitive & industry-aligned salary. 
 - Stable team culture with regular engagement activities. 
 - Flexible working hours and 5-day work week. 
 - On-time salary disbursement.

data.title: Software Product Assurance Engineer
data.description:
ReOrbit is looking for a motivated and detail oriented Software Product Assurance Engineer for Space Systems to join our growing team. 

As our new Software Product Assurance Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and safety of software throughout the spacecraft development lifecycle. You will define and evolve software product assurance requirements, adapted to lean and agile development practices, while applying a criticality-based approach where the level of rigour is aligned with the safety and mission impact of each software item. 

You will work closely with software, systems, hardware, AIT, Product Assurance and supplier teams to ensure that software development, verification, configuration management and change control activities meet the required quality and product assurance standards. 

It's an exciting chance to join a dynamic start-up, with the opportunity to make a real impact, to reach our goal of pushing the boundaries of space data transfer. 

Responsibilities

- Define and evolve software product assurance requirements across the development lifecycle, adapted to lean and agile development practices. 
 - Apply a criticality-based approach to software product assurance, scaling the level of rigour according to the safety and mission impact of the software item. 
 - Develop, implement, monitor and review Software Product Assurance (SW PA) plans. 
 - Oversee and participate in verification and validation (V&V) activities according to defined V&V plans. 
 - Support Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) activities, working with IV&V personnel to mitigate software risks and enhance safety and quality. 
 - Help drive internal and external reviews of development plans and software designs to ensure seamless integration with the satellite system. 
 - Participate in the analysis and evaluation of software designs, including change impact analysis and regression testing, particularly for COTS software. 
 - Support Product Assurance activities across engineering and flight models and associated infrastructure, ensuring documentation and objective evidence are captured consistently. 
 - Contribute to estimating and tracking the expected reliability and availability of the satellite platform as part of Product Assurance reporting. 
 - Support Product Assurance follow-up on supplier discrepancies and defects, ensuring corrective actions are documented and tracked. 
 - Support engineering change control, including understanding the Class I / Class II concept and ensuring the required approvals are obtained. 
 - Be willing to travel to supplier facilities for audits when required. 

Skills And Requirements

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in aerospace, electronics, information technology, systems engineering and minimum 8 years of work experience in a similar relevant field. 
 - Knowledge of software development processes and lifecycles. 
 - Knowledge of software verification techniques, including testing and inspections. 
 - Knowledge of software configuration management fundamentals and related tools. 
 - Clear conceptual understanding of the difference between proactive Product Assurance and retrospective Quality Control. 
 - Familiarity with non-conformances, deviations, waivers, and corrective/preventive actions, including RCA and CAPA, at a basic level. 
 - Awareness of SW Product Assurance principles and the ECSS/Q Product Assurance philosophy. 
 - Ability to constructively challenge engineering decisions and ask, "What is the risk?"
 - Comfortable working cross-functionally with systems, hardware, software, AIT and suppliers. 
 - Clear and effective technical writing and communication skills in English, both written and spoken. 
 - Previous exposure to satellite technologies through an internship, thesis, or student satellite project (e. g. CubeSat, nanosat or payloads), with an understanding of software Product Assurance concepts such as verification matrices, test coverage and configuration management. 
 - Introductory knowledge of risk management and single-point failure identification, with proficiency in C/C++ and Python and familiarity with NASA software assurance standards such as NASA-STD-8739. 8 and NASA-GB-8719. 13. 

What does ReOrbit do?

ReOrbit builds the foundation for the next generation of space applications by transforming satellites into truly intelligent, interconnected platforms, defined by software. Our satellite design philosophy revolves around the idea that satellites must network, communicate with each other and thus improve mission efficiency. How can this be achieved? Thanks to a flexible software-first architecture, where all these aspects are dealt with upfront in the mission concept, as integrated functionalities. 

ReOrbit's top-notch team of software engineers and system architects develop in-house software, procure hardware from the best-in-class suppliers, and seamlessly integrate the components to create flexible and secure satellites. Today, we are a rapidly growing company building a very strong multidisciplinary team to support our activities. We are headquartered in Helsinki, Finland with a subsidiaries in Bristol, UK, Bariloche, Argentina and Bengaluru, India. 

Working at ReOrbit

At ReOrbit, we are focused on building a strong team as we believe nothing can be accomplished without innovative, humble and curious minds working together on a common goal. We're all about fostering an inclusive, dynamic environment where equality and diversity are our strength. 

We offer

- Challenging but rewarding environment - you will thrive if you are always reflecting on how to make things better. Your ideas will be heard. 
 - Ambitious and supportive network of people, who are motivated to change the space industry, bringing expertise from both classic and new space . 
 - Benefits such as lunch vouchers, events, parties, occupational health care and additional health insurance - but most importantly a possibility to be a part of a unique and diverse team, connected by similar mindset and sense of humor. 
 - We like to spend time together! You can choose activities whichever is to your liking - runOrbit, climbOrbit; become ping pong or board games champion. 

Join us in our journey of building software enabled satellites for secure communications

and, thus, creating the most compelling in space data flow company of the new space era. 

The Company may require a security clearance for certain positions. Any such security clearance will be conducted in accordance with applicable law and the Company's relevant policies

For agencies: We do not accept unsolicited CVs for our open vacancies. Any CV sent to our team unsolicited will reserve us the right to pursue a candidate without obligation to the sender. All candidate submissions must be conducted through our official channels and in accordance with our terms of engagement.

data.title: FFR - Lead Software Engineer – Backend & AI/ML & Cloud
data.description:
FactSet creates flexible, open data and software solutions for over 200, 000 investment professionals worldwide, providing instant access to financial data and analytics that investors use to make crucial decisions. 

At FactSet, our values are the foundation of everything we do. They express how we act and operate, serve as a compass in our decision-making, and play a big role in how we treat each other, our clients, and our communities. We believe that the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere, at any time, and that curiosity is the key to anticipating our clients' needs and exceeding their expectations. 

Your Team's Impact

The team comprises highly motivated engineers and stakeholders who are passionate about extracting targeted insights from diverse document sources and transforming them into high-value data products. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies, the team focuses on building scalable pipelines that efficiently collect, structure, and process large volumes of data. 

Over time, the team has developed a robust and high-performing data pipeline capable of generating best-in-class structured datasets that power FactSet's products. Currently, the team is advancing this ecosystem by driving end-to-end automation across multiple stages of the pipeline. This includes the development of an event-driven, GenAI-centric, agent-based infrastructure aimed at enhancing efficiency, scalability, and innovation in data processing workflows. 

SUB-PROCESS BRIEF

Leads development strategies, architecture designs, data management, and code flow analysis necessary for the software development life cycle. Works closely with different groups/teams to ensure engineering team delivers on precision/correctness, performance, and scalability across our distributed computational framework. 

What You'll Do: -

- AI/ML & LLM Expertise: 
 - Design, fine-tune, and deploy small and open-source large language models (LLMs) such as Llama, Mistral, OpenAI GPT, etc. 
 - Hands-on leadership in prompt engineering, few-shot prompting, and building advanced NLP/NLU workflows. 
 - Guide adoption of modern AI/ML frameworks (Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain, LangGraph, etc. ) and architect reusable pipelines in Python. 
 - Python & API Development: 
 - Drive critical systems architecture in Python, using best practices in API and microservices design (FastAPI, Flask, Django, etc. ). 
 - Cloud Deployment (AWS/Azure/GCP): 
 - Architect, deploy, and scale robust, production-grade ML/AI solutions on cloud (AWS strongly preferred), leveraging cloud-native tools (Lambda, S3, ECS/ECR/Fargate, etc. ), serverless, and IaC (CloudFormation/Terraform). 
 - Champion DevOps best practices, automation, containerization (Docker/K8s), CI/CD, and operational monitoring. 
 - Technical Leadership: 
 - Mentor engineers, lead by example, drive system architecture reviews and code standards, and ensure high-quality technical delivery across teams. 
 - Act as the technical point of contact for escalation, incident resolution, and production troubleshooting. 
What We're Looking For: -

- Experience: 
 - 8-12 years in software development, including 3+ in senior or lead roles delivering ML/AI solutions in a cloud environment. 
 - LLM & Prompt Engineering: 
 - Strong real-world experience in LLM prompt engineering, few-shot prompting, and fine-tuning (using frameworks like Hugging Face, LangChain, LangGraph, etc. ). 
 - Python Expertise: 
 - Mastery of Python for API/microservice development, object-oriented patterns, code optimization, automated testing, and packaging. 
 - Cloud (AWS Preferred): 
 - Hands-on deployment and scaling of AI/ML services on AWS, Azure, or GCP; proficient in containers, serverless, and infrastructure as code. 
 - Technical Leadership: 
 - Proven experience mentoring software engineers, shaping system design, and driving cross-team initiatives. 
 - Communication: 
 - Exceptional ability to explain complex technical subjects and influence technical direction with diverse audiences. 
Nice to Have: -

- Databricks: 
 - Experience building, deploying, or orchestrating ML/AI or data pipelines on Databricks (Data Engineering, MLflow, collaborative workflows, jobs). 
 - (Note: Knowledge of Databricks is highly valued but not required; candidates without PySpark but with Databricks experience are welcome. )
 - PySpark: 
 - Experience using PySpark for big data ETL/processing, but not a must-have. 
 - Data Engineering: 
 - Familiarity with Spark, Airflow, advanced data analytics stacks, and modern data lakes (e. g. , Delta Lake). 
 - ML Productionization & MLOps: 
 - Experience with ML lifecycle tools, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and model governance. 
 - Visualization: 
 - Python-based dashboarding/analytics (Streamlit, Dash, Plotly). 
 - Security & Compliance: 
 - Secure cloud design, IAM, encryption, and compliance frameworks. 
 - Published Work / Open Source: 
 - Contributions to AI/ML communities, conference presentations, or technical publications. 
Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent. 
 - Experience working in product engineering organizations preferred. 

What's In It For You

At FactSet, our people are our greatest asset, and our culture is our biggest competitive advantage. Being a FactSetter means: 

- The opportunity to join an S&P 500 company with over 45 years of sustainable growth powered by the entrepreneurial spirit of a start-up. 
 - Support for your total well-being. This includes health, life, and disability insurance, as well as retirement savings plans and a discounted employee stock purchase program, plus paid time off for holidays, family leave, and company-wide wellness days. 
 - Flexible work accommodations. We value work/life harmony and offer our employees a range of accommodations to help them achieve success both at work and in their personal lives. 
 - A global community dedicated to volunteerism and sustainability, where collaboration is always encouraged, and individuality drives solutions. 
 - Career progression planning with dedicated time each month for learning and development. 
 - Business Resource Groups open to all employees that serve as a catalyst for connection, growth, and belonging. 

Learn More About Our Benefits Here. 

Salary is just one component of our compensation package and is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, and certifications. 

Company Overview

FactSet (NYSE: FDS | NASDAQ: FDS) helps the financial community to see more, think bigger, and work better. Our digital platform and enterprise solutions deliver financial data, analytics, and open technology to more than 8, 200 global clients, including over 200, 000 individual users. Clients across the buy-side and sell-side, as well as wealth managers, private equity firms, and corporations, achieve more every day with our comprehensive and connected content, flexible next-generation workflow solutions, and client-centric specialized support. As a member of the S&P 500, we are committed to sustainable growth and have been recognized among the Best Places to Work in 2023 by Glassdoor as a Glassdoor Employees' Choice Award winner. Learn more at www. factset. com and follow us on X and LinkedIn. 

At FactSet, we celebrate difference of thought, experience, and perspective. Qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to characteristics protected by law.

data.title: Senior Engineer -DFT
data.description:
Responsibilities

Architect, implement, and validate innovative DFT techniques on ARM SoCs. Insert DFT logic into SoC style designs at the RTL level and at the Synthesis gate level, validate all features, and generate ATE targeted test patterns to be run on silicon. Work closely with front-end design and verification teams on DFT RTL level insertion, back-end synthesis, place-and-route, and static-timing-analysis teams on gate level insertion and timing closure, and Test and Debug teams on silicon characterization and validation. 

Required Skills And Experience

- Core DFT skills considered for this position should include some of the following: Scan compression and insertion, Memory BIST and repair scheme implementation, Logic BIST, JTAG/IJTAG, at-speed test, ATPG, fault simulation, back-annotated gate level verification, silicon debug, memory and scan diagnostics
 - Experience ranges from 3- 20 Years. 
 - Experience coding Verilog RTL, TCL and/or Perl
 - Proficient in Unix/Linux environments
 - Bachelors or Master's degree or equivalent experience in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field

"Nice To Have" Skills and Experience : 

- Familiarity with IEEE 1149, 1500, 1687, 1838
 - Synthesis & Static Timing Analysis
 - Familiarity with SoC style architectures including multi-clock domain and low power design practices. 
 - Validated understanding of Siemens DFT tools
 - Familiarity with Arm IP like the following: Cortex CPUs, Mali GPUs, AMBA protocols, CoreLink interconnects, CoreSight debug
 - Experience with 2. 5D and 3D test
 - Ability to work both collaboratively on a team and independently
 - Hard-working and excellent time management skills with an ability to multi-task
 - An upbeat demeanor to working on exciting projects on the cutting edge of technology
 - Experience with Siemens, Cadence, and/or Synopsys DFT and simulation tools

Our 10x Mindset

At Arm, we believe progress happens when people are empowered to think bigger and push beyond what seems possible. Our 10x mindset is about curiosity, ambition and creating impact that will be used by millions. We learn fast, prioritise collaboration and turn bold ideas into real technology. All accommodation or adjustment requests will be treated with confidentiality, and information concerning these requests will only be disclosed as necessary to provide the accommodation. Although this is not an exhaustive list, examples of support include breaks between interviews, having documents read aloud, or office accessibility. Please email us about anything we can do to accommodate you during the recruitment process. 

Hybrid Working

Arm's approach to hybrid working is designed to create a working environment that supports both high performance and personal wellbeing. data.title: DCO Manager , Infra Ops - HYD
data.description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain - and we're looking for talented people who want to help. 

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. Data Center Manager for the world's biggest Cloud Infrastructure. 

You will be a proven manager with experience managing teams of high performers. You will have the ability to refine and develop processes to optimize operational excellence in every area of your role. You will be able to drive performance levels to achieve the pace at which we build and operate Data Centers in India for Amazon Data Services India Private Limited ("ADSIPL"). You will have previous experience in Data Centers, either building or managing (or both) along with exposure to developing great relationships with both internal teams and external vendors. 

You will also have a passion for technology along with a desire to be the best at your job every day!

Key job responsibilities

As a Data Center Manager in ADSIPL, you will get to manage the world's largest Cloud Computing Infrastructure in India. We encounter interesting, challenging & complex problems every day, being a technical manager in ADSIPL means that you can innovate to solve these issues and help drive Operations Excellence in all areas of your role. 

Your day job at ADSIPL will include (but not limited to): 

- Managing and developing teams of high quality Data Center Technicians, providing both technical and leadership expertise and ensuring highest levels of performance. 
 - Maintaining existing co-located and in-house Data Centers in India
 - Helping build and bring online new Data Centers in India
 - Constantly improving all our processes and procedures. We believe there is nothing we cannot improve
 - Assisting & managing relationships with external vendors & contractors
 - Liaising with internal teams & management groups at ADSIPL
 - Ensuring we adhere to and exceed local Health & Safety standards in all our Data Centers in India
 - Creating and maintaining metrics on all aspects of ADSIPL's Data Centers in India and utilizing those metrics to drive positive changes
 - Assisting in implementing service methodologies including incident management, problem management, change management, capacity management, etc. 

A day in the life

Managing and developing teams of high quality Data Center Technicians, providing both technical and leadership expertise and ensuring highest levels of performance. 

- Maintaining existing co-located and in-house Data Centers in India
 - Helping build and bring online new Data Centers in India

About The Team

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying. 

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating - that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do. 

Mentorship and Career Growth

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. 

Basic Qualifications

- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in software development and experience in technical support
 - 7+ years of operations management experience
 - 5+ years of managing technical teams with significant personnel management experience and examples of developing engineers and building successful teams experience
 - Experience in facilities management

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) field, or 3+ months of network and operating system support experience
 - 2+ years of Agile methods and processes experience
 - Knowledge of six Sigma/Lean processes
 - Experience creating and implementing large-scale programs
 - 1+ years of capacity planning, operations planning, business analysis or similar experience

data.description:
